newsitem.title: JAPAN: US says accord likely with Japan on reform talks.
newsitem.headline: US says accord likely with Japan on reform talks.

text.p: The United States and Japan are likely to reach an agreement on a new format for their talks on deregulation by next week's G7 summit in Denver, a U.S. official said on Thursday.
"I am encouraged from today's discussions that we will be successful in reaching an agreement by the G7 summit," the official told reporters after one day of talks with Japanese officials.

Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto and President Bill Clinton agreed in Washington in late April on the need to intensify the bilateral dialogue on deregulation, which has been conducted under the 1993 U.S.-Japan Framework Agreement.
The two are expected to hold a bilateral meeting on the sidelines of the Group of Seven (G7) industrial nations summit from June 20-22.
The official said the enhanced initiative on deregulation will benefit Japanese consumers and increase access of foreign firms to the Japanese market.
The U.S. put forward a new proposal on Thursday which is based on their first proposal presented to Japan last month calling for the establishment periodic meetings by senior officials.
The official said Japan has also made some proposals on the talks, and there was "sufficient overlapping" between the Japanese and U.S. proposals.
The new U.S. proposal also says that initial discussions should focus on housing, medical equipment, pharmaceuticals, telecommunications and financial services.
The areas for discussion would be expanded in the future, the official said. He said power generation is one area "that deserves consideration".
The U.S. has also proposed setting up expert groups to discuss structural issues such as distribution and transparencey in government practices.
